title: How the ankle supports walking
intro: The ankle links the lower leg with the foot, carrying weight while adapting to the ground. Its joints, ligaments, tendons and muscles work together; pain after a twist is not automatically a minor sprain.

sections.heading: Bones and movement
paragraphs: The tibia and fibula surround the talus. This upper joint mainly moves the foot up and down; lower joints contribute to side-to-side adaptation.

sections.heading: Smooth contact
paragraphs: Cartilage and joint fluid reduce friction. Joint shape helps distribute load, but repeated force beyond tissue tolerance can still cause injury.

sections.heading: Stability
paragraphs: Ligaments connect bones and limit excessive movement. Tendons transmit muscle force; the Achilles tendon helps push off. A ligament injury differs from a tendon rupture or fracture.

sections.heading: Recovery and activity
paragraphs: After injury, protect the ankle and seek advice about safe loading. Gradual strength and balance work may help recovery; repeated giving-way deserves review rather than repeated forced stretching.

sections.heading: Warning signs
paragraphs: Deformity, inability to bear weight, a cold or numb foot, or a sudden snap with loss of push-off needs prompt assessment. Being able to move the ankle does not exclude a fracture.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira repeatedly rolls an ankle on uneven ground. She asks about rehabilitation and balance rather than using a support as the whole solution.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben feels a snap while running and cannot push off. He seeks assessment instead of walking it off as a routine sprain.
